propositions: The gate matches field names globally using bare attribute names anywhere under src/rebar, so a field name reused on any unrelated config object passes the gate even if that field itself is never read.

CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because .enabled was read on unrelated configs (UiConfig.enabled, McpConfig.auth_enabled, etc.), while uniquely-named CodeHealthConfig.analyzers correctly tripped the gate.

Common field names (enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, mode) that are reused across configs cannot be policed by the current gate due to bare-name matching, creating a false-negative class for the inert-config family it exists to prevent.

The fixed gate must resolve reads to the owning dataclass via six resolution routes (section-attribute names, annotations, local assignment propagation, return annotations, conditionals, and cross-module call-site binding) rather than testing bare name membership.

Four fields newly flagged by the corrected gate (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) are all live and read through documented indirection, and must receive accurate # read-via: markers naming their actual readers.
